name: Dahi Bara Aloo Dum
instructions: 1. Soak urad dal for 4-6 hours, grind to a smooth fluffy batter, and deep fry small portions into golden brown fritters.
2. Soak the fried fritters in warm water for 10 minutes, squeeze gently, then submerge them in spiced buttermilk seasoned with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and ginger.
3. Prepare the Aloo Dum by sautéing ginger-garlic paste, onions, and spices (turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala) before adding boiled potatoes and simmering with tamarind water.
4. To serve, place 3-4 dahi baras on a plate, pour a generous ladle of aloo dum over them.
5. Top with chopped onions, fresh coriander, sev, and a dash of black salt.
description: Dahi Bara Aloo Dum is the hallmark of Odia street food, particularly famous in the city of Cuttack. It is a unique combination of cool, soothing dahi baras and spicy, tangy potato curry, reflecting the distinct flavor profiles of Eastern Indian cuisine.
